content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge uses Matthew 1:16's not stating the begetter in either direction as the ground for UNDERDETERMINED, which is a single-verse ruling.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.","room":"does not apply when the judge weighs two chains — reading one: this text decides Matthew 1:16 as a single verse, so K-S2 applies; reading two: the reference to the defender's prior answers means two chains are weighed, so K-S2 would not apply.","why":"The judge's stated ground for UNDERDETERMINED is that Matthew 1:16's own words do not state the begetter in either direction, which K-S2 forbids as a ground."}
